# R319 — Current production fixed-history scoring hook

Date: 2026-10-13 (JST). Read-only source design audit of the current curated W source (parent supplied clean HEAD `e3c904e2`; no Git command was run), prior quality-hook reports, and primary inference/evaluation implementations. No implementation, import, test, build, GPU/model/profiler/process work, Git operation, cleanup, or active Main long128 receipt was accessed. This report specifies a usable quality-only path; it is not a qualification or a request to run it.

## Finding

The current W standalone native generator already has the smallest fixed-history/full-logit path: combine `--spec-follow` with `--dump-logits`, and constrain its decode windows so only rows whose preceding inputs match the reference continuation are emitted/committed. With a native pack, batched prompt, no `--serve`, a supplied follow sequence of exactly N token IDs, and `--max-new N`, the native path's first verifier input is the final prompt token. `--spec-follow` substitutes the fixed reference token for each row's argmax and the existing verifier acceptance loop commits only the contiguous prefix of draft inputs that matches those forced IDs. `--dump-logits` writes each emitted row's full float32 vocabulary logits. Therefore, for every emitted row i, its previous verifier inputs are exactly the prompt suffix followed by `follow[0..i-1]`, and its full distribution can be scored against `follow[i]`.

This reuses production `Prefill`, `Verifier::run`, `Verifier::commit`, native head and kernel dispatch; it needs no new inference API or code path for standalone `generate`. It is opt-in instrumentation and **must be run separately** from the quiet performance measurement. A full-vocabulary copy/write affects timing, and this standalone contract does not claim API `--serve` overhead or server-loop behavior. If the result must certify `--serve` specifically, this is not enough: add a default-off serve request field to force a fixed continuation and write full target rows at the serving verifier seam, then validate live-session reuse and boundaries separately.

## Current source contract and state boundaries

Source reviewed: `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/perf-native-copy-cohorts-qualified-20261012/src/program/generate.cpp`, `src/core/verify.cpp`, and `include/strata/core/verify.hpp`.

1. For a native prompt of P IDs, standalone `generate.cpp:10383–10416` sends `P-1` IDs `[0,P-2]` through `prefill.run`; the last prompt token at index/position `P-1` remains in `tok`. It seeds `ss.ple_prev` from prompt IDs `P-3,P-2` before that final prompt token is processed. Native packs skip the standalone ordinary-token generation loop and enter the verifier path with `first_window=true`; the first verifier window is forced to T=1 (`:10433`, speculative loop `:10867–10910`). Thus predictor row 0 consumes prompt[P-1] and scores target follow[0].
2. `Verifier::run(T, window, p, ...)` stages input tokens and absolute positions and computes per-row PLE inputs (`verify.cpp:1441–1505`). `read_logits(rows, ...)` copies complete head rows (`:1759–1765`). The run synchronizes its stream before return (also noted by the existing `window_logprobs` contract at `:2335`).
3. After run, `generate.cpp:10951–10959` overwrites `outv` with the fixed follow IDs, then computes `a` as the longest contiguous equality between proposed window input `window[i+1]` and forced output `outv[i]`. It commits `a+1` rows (`:10970`). The emitted rows are exactly indices 0 through a; the verifier row i is valid for reference history because every prior proposed token in that row's prefix matched the fixed continuation. On mismatch, later speculative rows are discarded. The next verifier `x` and position advance from the last committed forced ID (`:11020+`; commit logic at `verify.cpp:2384–2403`). This retains the actual causal KV and GDN state; it does not need to recompute the 32K prefix for each token.
4. When a one-token commit is used, `Verifier::commit` updates PLE predecessor state from the committed token; multirow commit keeps its accepted prefix. Do not separately advance or overwrite KV/GDN/PLE state in a host-side scorer. The first continuation row is at absolute predictor position `P-1`; row i is at `P-1+i` and scores follow[i]. Exactly N rows cover positions `[P-1, P+N-2]`. Require `P + N - 1 <= max_context` and respect any stricter source/window/capacity constraints.
5. `--dump-logits` establishes `dump_first=P-1`, and native row count is `max_new` (`generate.cpp:4939–4963`). In the verify path, only emitted rows are copied/written, with row index derived from absolute p (`:10990–11006`). The binary format starts with two int32s `{vocab, rows}` followed by row-major float32 logits. For exact full-distribution scoring set `--logits-stride 1` (default); stride >1 is restricted to `--max-new 1` (`:2785`). The file's number of rows must equal N and byte length must equal `8 + 4 * vocab * N`.

A bounded current-route command shape is therefore:

```text
strata generate <same model/native/profile/KV/cache/prefill/runtime args as the target route>
  --tokens-file prompt.ids --max-new N --spec <same supported verifier setting>
  --spec-follow follow.ids --dump-logits candidate.logits
```

Keep all baseline/candidate weights, tokenizer, PLE, cache/profile, KV/context, experts/routes, build/compiler/runtime, and prompt/follow token IDs identical; change only the optimized kernel/source arm. If isolating the target model from speculative-drafter behavior, run both arms with MTP absent and suffix/lookup drafts disabled; for a production-MTP quality comparison, retain identical MTP artifacts/settings and treat it as an additional arm. In either case, proposal acceptance affects only how many matched rows can be verified together; it cannot change the reference inputs of emitted rows. Preserve the production prefill settings: the fixed-history mode must not change chunk size, short-read routing, or PLE mode to make capture easier.

## Strict wrapper/admission checks needed

The present CLI has two silent-shortening / invalid-input hazards that a quality wrapper must reject before engine work:

- `--max-new` controls the logits header, while `--spec-follow` is internally truncated to `min(--max-new, follow.size())` (`generate.cpp:10662–10668`). Require exact follow length N and set `--max-new N`; otherwise header rows and written rows can disagree.
- `read_ids` parses the follow file but does not enforce exactly N IDs or check each ID against `0..n_vocab-1`. Preparse and validate all IDs and file/hash/count before startup. A missing, empty, malformed, out-of-range, or truncated sequence must fail closed; empty follow disables forcing and falls back to normal decode. Require normal completion and exact N output/dump rows.

Also reject `--serve` (source help expressly documents `--spec-follow` as standalone only), EOS stopping / configured early stop, cancellation, `--prefill-until`, stride >1, and incompatible oracle/corruption/draft behavior. Check the actual `follow` mismatch/emitted counts, exit status, output and logits file sizes, finite every logit, no verifier/pool/queue/runtime fault, and complete row coverage. Set greedy for reproducibility of the irrelevant argmax side channel; it does not define the forced targets. `--spec-follow` reports how many forced IDs differed from argmax; that count is expected to be nonzero and is not a quality failure.

Quality capture itself must be kept outside quiet timing and have a declared `N * vocab * 4` byte budget before launch; stream rows to an owned, single-purpose file if the full artifact fits. For paired metrics, normalize the complete row with stable log-sum-exp in higher precision, then record target NLL, top-1/top-2 and margin, target rank, KL between full baseline/candidate distributions, and per-position error summaries. A full trace is retained only through verified metric/hash production and then retired under the retention manifest, unless a current named numerical investigation still consumes it.

This only scores distributions after the actual candidate batched prompt and verifier state. The batched-prefill synchronization/runtime path must already be admitted for the exact machine/configuration. `--spec-follow` does not make an unsafe prefill route safe; do not invoke it on an unqualified route or let the quality dump contaminate timing claims. No model input below 32K is in scope.

## Fit with upstream scoring designs

- **vLLM:** its `prompt_token_id_logprobs` interface accepts candidate token IDs per row and scores chosen target IDs during one prefill. The documented row convention maps row i to prediction of prompt token `prompt_logprob_start+i+1`, and its teacher-scoring guide says to start at prompt length minus one for response scoring. It skips prefix cache for this operation because cached rows have no logits. This is a clear position-alignment precedent; it returns selected token scores rather than a full distribution. See [vLLM prompt-token scoring](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/training/prompt_token_id_logprobs/) and [API shape/row convention](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/api/vllm/).
- **llama.cpp:** `llama-perplexity` scores corpus tokens and supports storing base logits to a `.kld` file, then comparing candidate-model logits/KL. It is a useful artifact/metric precedent for full distributions but not a live-cache verifier transaction contract. See [llama.cpp perplexity/KL guide](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/examples/model-conversion/README.md) and [perplexity tool guide](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/perplexity/README.md).
- **SGLang:** its `/generate` scoring interface uses `return_logprob`, `logprob_start_len`, and `top_logprobs_num`, and returns input token logprobs/optional top candidates. This is a teacher-scoring API precedent for selected IDs, not evidence of a full-vocabulary logit dump. See [SGLang runtime endpoint](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/lang/backend/runtime_endpoint.py).

These APIs inform interface shape and position semantics; they do not supply Strata's GDN/KV commit rules or justify comparing only generated strings.

## Why `serve` needs a separate hook if that is the target

W `serve` has its own request loop (`generate.cpp:8116+`, first prompt decode at `:9206+`, verifier loop at `:9780+`); it parses `GEN` requests and optionally returns the generated token's scalar log-probability plus top-K candidates (`:8145–8169`, `:9901–9925`). It exposes no `--dump-logits` on request, and the current endpoint computes logprob for `outv[i]`, not an arbitrary teacher token, so it cannot directly return full distributions for a fixed reference history. Repeated one-token GEN requests with a growing reference prompt could reuse a session only if every `RESUME` exactly equals the prior committed token boundary; it still does not provide full-vocab rows and adds request-boundary complexity. The safer minimum server extension would be a default-off scoring mode in the existing serial verifier loop: accept a validated fixed follow list, perform the normal prompt read once, use the same verifier windows/accept-prefix commit logic, capture full logits for emitted fixed rows before they are overwritten, and write row positions/target IDs/coverage. It must reject speculative pipeline mode until its forced-prefix state/rollback path is explicitly covered, and it must not alter ordinary GEN behavior when off.

## Evidence reviewed and limits

- Current W source files/line locations above; no Git command was used. Parent supplied W clean revision identity `e3c904e2`.
- R316 `research-xe-b9-numerical-route-divergence-round316-v1.txt`: b9 output divergence is not a quality result; fixed-history full-row comparison is needed.
- R318 `research-llm-numerical-quality-acceptance-policy-round318-v1.txt`: quality metrics, A/A calibration, separate task-quality and runtime gates.
- R336 `round336-native-decode-teacherforce-existing-interface-contract.txt`: prior audit said serving APIs do not expose arbitrary fixed-token full distributions; this pass narrows the distinction: standalone `--spec-follow` plus `--dump-logits` can satisfy the fixed-history use case because the accepted-prefix loop is causal, while `--serve` still cannot.
- R297 `round297-compiled-generator-quality-hook-provenance-correction.txt`: existing `STRATA_LOGPOS` is limited to verifier-window prompt scoring, while `STRATA_DUMP_FIRST_LOGITS` is one row; neither alone covers a fixed post-prefill continuation.

No fixture was executed, no feature was implemented, and no model/route was validated. Before relying on the existing standalone flags, source/build provenance and exact N-row output/index coverage must be checked on a closed admitted run. Do not infer that a successful quality-path run is a quiet performance result or current Main run status.
